$comment: Canonical framework patches, shipped with the CLI and registered at the workspace root by xplat patches apply for Bun or pnpm. bun run sync:patches updates root Bun registrations, the patch package, and pnpm starter configuration; bun run check:patches rejects drift. Maintain patches with bun patch and bun patch --commit, retaining the canonical file path and updating why/dropWhen. bunSpecifiers names exact Bun source identities when tarball dependencies differ from pnpm version identities. repository: false retains a consumer patch without registering it in this repository. template: false excludes a patch from pnpm starter configuration.

patches.why: Published 0.16.3 includes universal Children normalization, descriptorChildren and their compiler allowlist entries, plus compiler-owned generic binding bags. Retains universal signal-read tracking and local hooks, root event-error forwarding, the complete universal imperative-ref lifecycle, the Descriptor declaring-owner reader fallback, and the signal-owner/enclosingOwner chain so child reads reuse instance declarations. Preserves keyed component ownership through compiler-generated transparent root slots so native map reorders retain host identity, state, and portal content. Rebased against the registry 0.16.3 tarball; upstream Children and binding-bag implementations are preserved. Also normalizes `queueRefAttach`'s scope-or-block argument — descriptor host mounts pass the owner Block through `setHostProps`, leaving queued ref attaches with `block: undefined` and crashing `drainQueuedRefAttaches` in `comparePostOrder`. Adds __methodDep to the universal compiler UNIVERSAL_RUNTIME_IMPORTS allowlist so universal targets can compile member calls inside hook callbacks (x.m() in useMemo/useCallback); universal-core already exports the helper. Universal HMR slot keys chain the previously resolved hook key into the slot path, so slot identity is sequence-dependent: an unchanged hook signature reuses its records in place, while a shifted signature resolves fresh slots that cannot inherit another hook's value (the 498eb3f1e revision-keyed remount is retired in favor of this collision-safe identity). Universal HMR accepted updates invoke the revised component in place again, restoring retained view/state semantics. withSlot unwraps UNIVERSAL_HMR bindings so compiler-emitted hook calls execute the current revision.
patches.dropWhen: An octane release (0.15.0+) exports universal Children normalization and descriptorChildren and accepts both in the universal compiler, integrates universal signal reads/local hooks and owner ancestry, forwards uncaught event-handler errors, and supports optional/replaced/nested imperative refs with callback cleanup. Generic binding bags must also participate in transaction-fragment parent rehoming. Universal array reconciliation must also preserve component keys through transparent root-slot wrappers. Ref-attach queueing must also tolerate callers passing the owning Block instead of a Scope. An octane release whose universal compiler admits __methodDep in UNIVERSAL_RUNTIME_IMPORTS also retires the added hunk. An octane release with signature-aware universal HMR (or equivalent collision-safe slot identity) retires the slot-chain hunk. An octane release whose universal HMR wrapper does not intercept direct calls inside render attempts retires the withSlot hunk.

patches.why: Published 9.1.3 ships the #11446 nested-tab-frame lifecycle fix and iOS explicit-size flex alignment, so those hunks are removed. Retains the unshipped parent-padding measure-spec fix and Android explicit-size flex alignment, iOS continuous corner clipping, CSS @layer cascade support, custom Android variable-font weight mapping, computed iOS variable-font weight resolution with explicit-axis precedence and axis-aware caching, and percentage translate parsing, native view, and animation support. Backports NativeScript#11527 and the variable-substitution portion of #11593: complete nested fallbacks, initial as guaranteed-invalid, whole-value invalidation, forward custom-property references, null invalid variables, and resetting failed setter updates without caching them. The separate invalid color-mix converter repair from #11593 is not included. Verified against the registry 9.1.3 tarball; it has no Windows implementation, so the separate Windows preview patch remains.
patches.dropWhen: A published @nativescript/core release contains the remaining flexbox measure/alignment, continuous corners, cascade layers, custom Android and computed iOS variable-font weight mapping, and percentage-translate fixes (NativeScript/NativeScript#11481), plus CSS variable fallback/settling/reset semantics from #11527 and the variable-substitution portion of #11593.

patches.why: On iOS, a nested foreign RootLayout can retain its preceding exact frame as an intrinsic minimum, preventing a same-cell Grid layer from shrinking. Before an outer Mason View/Scroll root measures, refresh nested foreign roots deepest-first with both axes unconstrained and invalidate their cached engine leaf measurements. Roots inside a Mason ancestor skip the warmup so native measurement callbacks do not re-enter the shared Rust compute. No frame or style height is pinned; the maintained foreign-screen-height resize assertions remain unchanged.
patches.dropWhen: An upstream Mason core release refreshes or invalidates nested foreign-root intrinsic measurements before outer layout and passes the maintained iOS same-cell Screen resize sequence, including 200x500 to 107x300, without this warmup.

patches.why: @nativescript/vite serializes bundled CSS and dev app.css through reworkcss `css`@3.0.0, which mis-parses @layer into garbage selectors — rules die before reaching _populateRules. Adds atlayer() covering block and statement forms. Applies to a transitive dep — no app declares it directly.
patches.dropWhen: npm `css` is unmaintained — drop when @nativescript/vite's serializer stops using it (e.g. pointed at NS's vendored css/lib/parse; NativeScript#11462)

patches.why: Remaining dev-server fixes on @nativescript/vite 8.0.20: classify only the requested vendor entry under active native ESM conditions, keeping mixed source-root/compiled-subpath packages on the Vite transform path; collect re-export specifiers in the .vite/deps rewrite; route outside-roots /@fs paths through /ns/m; probe non-active platform and native suffixes; redirect bare octane to octane/universal/native in deps-bundle esbuild passes; give library files served per-module on first boot static /ns/m vendor imports so ESM evaluation order and live bindings hold, keeping package-internal non-entry files concrete instead of folding them onto the package root (first-boot `Class extends value …` in gesturehandler); canonicalize /@fs pnpm virtual-store paths onto the vendor route's `/ns/m/node_modules/<pkg>` spelling when the store and root-resolved package share a realpath, so a package's modules can't split into two registries (first-boot `is not a registered element` in octane's element registry); add .mobile to tsconfig-paths and generated checker suffixes; scan the app-local pnpm virtual store for served node_modules URLs; ignore per-package turbo.json as workspace markers; resolve # package-imports specifiers in served-module rewrites; preserve, compile, and hot-update virtual stylesheets (NativeScript#11551); and inspect ESM export declarations/specifiers for native default-import validation instead of matching comments, strings, or a narrow export syntax (NativeScript#11566). Shared-source graph and hot-context IDs now use the same app/workspace/@fs paths as served imports, preserving distinct roots (NativeScript#11569); extensionless workspace requests probe filesystem-anchored extension/platform candidates so hot reimports can fetch shared modules (NativeScript#11570). Linked-checkout discovery and candidate anchoring shipped in 8.0.20 (NativeScript#11559), so those local hunks are removed. Vite `resolve.alias` entries are captured in configResolved and replayed inside the NativeScript esbuild passes (deps bundle, vendor bundle) via an esbuild alias plugin with @rollup/plugin-alias semantics, so Vite resolve.alias redirects for packages that are not installed (e.g. the renderer's full-MasonKit imports mapped to Mason core) resolve to real files instead of throw-on-evaluate optional-dependency stubs, while installed packages keep their default resolution; presence ignores pnpm's hidden `.pnpm/node_modules` hoist, so another workspace app's hoisted copy (apps/windows' full MasonKit) does not disable the alias; the deps-bundle disk cache key fingerprints the captured aliases. The runtime-plugin bare-specifier fold locates a package's package.json through Node's node_modules ancestor chain instead of a literal projectRoot/node_modules join, so deep `pkg/dist/...` specifiers fold back to the bare vendor id in hoisted workspaces where the app's own node_modules is empty (a missed fold leaves the vendor registry without the specifier and device require resolves a module missing the vendored exports). The bare-specifier HTTP fallback anchors at the importer's real path and walks its node_modules ancestors when the spec is absent from the app root chain, so a package present only as an importer's pnpm sibling (storybook's @storybook/global) rewrites to a serving /ns/m/@fs URL instead of the root-resolved /ns/m/node_modules/<spec> 404. The ALWAYS_INCLUDE presence check walks the filesystem node_modules ancestors instead of require.resolve, so NODE_PATH injected by pnpm bin shims cannot expose the hidden `.pnpm/node_modules` hoist and collect a package the app does not actually have (stacktrace-js via the workspace's firebase-crashlytics). Selects the explicit typescript-classic API alias for NativeClass lowering and config parsing when the project uses native TypeScript 7. Rejects a native launcher without a classic API instead of crashing on missing compiler methods; TSRX checks still delegate to the project checker. The /ns/m pipeline also fingerprints each resolved node_modules file at serve time (mtime+size) and purges Vite’s module graph plus the shared transform cache when the on-disk bytes drift, so pnpm/bun patch installs of source-served dependencies reach the device without a server restart. Additionally fixes deps-bundle ESM classification: the line-anchored syntax check misclassified minified .js ESM (`...;export{x as y};`) as opaque CJS, so the served shim dropped every named export (octane-xplat#181). maskJsComments gains a literals mode that also blanks string/template/regex interiors — with template ${} nesting honored — and the export scanners run on the masked copy, so mid-line ESM is found without matching ESM-looking text inside literals or comments. Mid-line `export * from`/`export * as ns` are followed too (specifier read back from the original text), and the keyword lookbehind keeps `$export`/`obj.import` member text from classifying CJS as ESM. Additionally owns the runtime’s deliberate dev-reload import cancellation: ns:module invalidateModules rejects every pending dynamic import() of an evicted module with `Module invalidated during dev reload: <url>`, and an entry `void import(...)` in flight during a whole-graph eviction surfaced as a fatal unhandled rejection (octane-xplat#188). hot-context.js installs an unhandledrejection filter that preventDefaults only that exact reason; genuine module/execution failures still report.
patches.dropWhen: Upstream classifies requested vendor entries under active ESM conditions (including mixed source-root/compiled-subpath exports), and ships the remaining re-export, outside-roots /@fs, platform/native candidate, deps-bundle alias, .mobile suffix (checker: NativeScript#11480), app-local pnpm store, turbo.json workspace-marker, # package-imports, virtual stylesheet fixes (NativeScript#11551), accurate default-export link validation (NativeScript#11566), shared-source HMR identity preservation (NativeScript#11569), extensionless workspace fetching (NativeScript#11570), main-realm package-internal file preservation (upstream fixed only the worker realm), and pnpm virtual-store /@fs canonicalization onto vendor-route URLs. Upstream esbuild dev passes honor Vite resolve.alias. Upstream resolves installed package metadata through ancestor node_modules for the exports reverse map. The compiler-API selection hunk retires when NativeScript supports a native compiler project without requiring the legacy TypeScript API from that same package name. The dep-freshness hunk retires when upstream watches or fingerprints node_modules files for the /ns/m transform caches. Upstream must also classify ESM anywhere on a line (NativeScript#11621) without literal/comment false positives and follow mid-line star re-exports. Upstream must also own or stop emitting the deliberate invalidateModules cancellation rejection so unhandled dynamic-import cancellations during dev reload are not reported as fatal (octane-xplat#188).

patches.why: Driver treats a prop dropped from an update's complete prop bag — or set to `undefined`/`null` — as a removal and restores the documented default: Property/CssProperty setters get `unsetValue`, plain fields restore the captured pre-prop value, and applied `style` keys diff per key. A never-applied `undefined` still skips the write since NativeScript native setters coerce it (e.g. editable → ios.userInteractionEnabled = NO). Aligns intrinsic ref types with Octane callback cleanup and nested arrays with optional entries. Advertises the implemented visibility capability so committed suspense bodies can be retained while pending. Preserves authored Grid row/col/span metadata independently of NativeScript defaults and computed auto-placement, notifying Grid when placement props change.
patches.dropWhen: @nativescript-community/octane ships removal-reset prop semantics, the undefined-skip, visibility capability, Octane-compatible intrinsic ref types, and Grid authored placement metadata with change notifications upstream.

patches.why: Retains the workspace's NativeScript driver fixes when upgrading to 0.2.5 for portal support: a prop dropped from an update's complete prop bag — or set to `undefined`/`null` — is a removal that restores the documented default (Property/CssProperty setters get `unsetValue`, plain fields the captured pre-prop value, `style` keys diff per key); a never-applied `undefined` still skips the write. Synced with PR #14: registered setters are identified before resetting (ordinary fields never receive the sentinel), inline removal refreshes matching class CSS through the isolated core 9.1 `_cssState.onChange` hook, CSS variables use public removal, strings use the core CSS parser, and replacement views capture fresh defaults. Also advertises the implemented visibility capability, carries Octane callback ref types, and preserves authored Grid row/col/span metadata. Hosts custom-layout containers (e.g. MasonKit ViewBase) that own child lists via insertChild/removeChild/getChildrenCount without subclassing LayoutBase. Additionally, the masonry cutover: masonview resolves to MasonKit View and scrollview to MasonKit Scroll as the only layout containers, with zero layout props — every former prop name warns-and-drops and all CSS semantics arrive through the style bag; foreign native leaves mirror resolved class and inline layout styles through Style.fromView, observe longhand changes and native recreation, and explicitly clear removed placement — removal restores the CSS cascade, so a later sibling attachment cannot resurrect removed tracks. Container alignment uses the core stretch default without a local style override, allowing class-authored centering. Inline style resets reapply the matching CSS cascade. Re-exports Octane's ClassValue unchanged and stringifies truthy numeric class values while omitting 0 and NaN, matching Octane 0.11. Maps collapsed foreign native leaves to Mason display:none, restoring effective display on visibility changes so both layout hosts omit the same item (#45). Adds observeBatches(): willApply/didApply batch observers on every NativeScript root (including nested applies, with depth) so layout projection can snapshot before and commit after each host batch, which a rerender-driven signal cannot cover on keyed reorder. Text hosts fold mixed children into one ordered FormattedString: `Span` under a TextBase auto-wraps into `formattedText`, and `#text` under FormattedString/Span folds to text — including driver-minted spans interleaved in child order — so nested styled runs and surrounding sibling text compose (xplat decisions #25).
patches.dropWhen: The upstream driver hosts Mason containers, preserves removal-reset semantics, and synchronizes resolved foreign-leaf layout styles with class/inline precedence and native-view lifecycle support. Foreign leaf visibility must also remove collapsed items from Mason layout and restore their effective display. Upstream ships a batch observer. Upstream also ships the text-fold: span-under-TextBase auto-wrapping and #text folding under FormattedString/Span.

patches.why: octaneServerStrategy's SCRIPT_FILE_RE only covers [jt]sx? — .tsrx edits never emit the deferred ns:hmr-delta broadcast, so component HMR silently never reaches the device. Also counts open /ns-hmr sockets so the update summary stops reporting recipients=0 for delivered updates. Includes shared script sources in transaction ordering while excluding dependencies, tests and declarations. External-source edits use the absolute source for graph identity and a Vite /@fs transform URL instead of treating parent-relative paths as app URLs.
patches.dropWhen: vite-octane release adds .tsrx matching and uses canonical graph IDs with filesystem transform URLs for external sources

Vendor-manifest gating and percent-decoded module paths are now upstream and no longer patched. Mid-line `export * from`/`export * as ns` are followed too (specifier read back from the original text), and the keyword lookbehind keeps `$export`/`obj.import` member text from classifying CJS as ESM. patches.dropWhen: windows moves off the preview pin — the real fix lands upstream with the windows platform merge (NativeScript#11272/#11468); retain the vendor collector repair until an adopted upstream release classifies the requested export under the native bundler conditions. The compiler-API selection hunk retires when NativeScript supports a native compiler project without requiring the legacy TypeScript API from that same package name. Upstream must also classify ESM anywhere on a line (NativeScript#11621) without literal/comment false positives and follow mid-line star re-exports. patches.why: Windows preview abae298 from NativeScript#11272 retains CSS @layer cascade machinery and explicit-size flex alignment, Windows pointer subscription and hover ownership, cancellation/capture-loss handling and gesture separation, parent-driven percentage sizing lifecycle and padded content-box updates, raw keyDown/keyUp subscription ownership, submit cancellation, and input focus/blur ownership, IsEnabled forwarding, accessible names, secure readonly, and literal non-CSS property values. Also moves _ensureNativeTransforms into a leaf module to break the view-common/animation import cycle that crashed ESM bundle evaluation at startup. The #11446 frame/tab fixes are now upstream and removed. Preserves upstream transparent-background hit testing and contact-only pointer moves. Registry core 9.1.4-next.0 has no Windows implementation; this patch targets the commit-pinned preview with that version. Uses the explicit NSWinRT.dotnet.invoke bridge for synchronous existence, recursive directory creation, and nontruncating OpenOrCreate file creation, preserving Core's System import shim. Existence projection failures are not treated as missing paths. Adds Windows single-contact pan with cumulative logical-DIP deltas, owned pointer capture, cancellation, and cleanup while retaining sibling touch delivery. Exposes the shared native event subscription registry through __xplatWindowsEvents so optional leaves reuse the host owner without deep-importing a second core module. Owns fixed legacy Flexbox child dimensions as preferred native inputs, with per-child style listeners, removal/disposal restoration and native-identity guards. This requires the matching app-local x64 Widgets repair; original binaries retain their prior behavior. Gives the Windows View declaration an unknown symbol index so generated native-property setter unions do not make layout subclasses structurally incompatible with View; named public property types stay checked. Completes the preview's partial CSS variable repair with null invalid custom-property values, a guarded initial check, and whole-value invalidation from NativeScript#11527 and the variable portion of #11593; existing fallback and failed-setter fixes are retained.
patches.dropWhen: A published Windows-capable core contains the retained cascade, layout, pointer, input, filesystem, and Windows declaration-assignability repairs. Source repairs remain in tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-pointer-core.patch, tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-layout/core-percent-source.patch, tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-input-core.patch, tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-module-cycle.patch, and tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-keyboard/. Filesystem artifact repair and qualification boundaries are recorded in .agents/docs/parity/windows-support-progress.md. The release must also emit cumulative Windows pan deltas with capture-loss cancellation and lifecycle cleanup; bounded x64 mouse evidence and remaining hardware-touch gates are in .agents/docs/parity/windows-support-progress.md. The release must also preserve fixed Flexbox requested sizes while arranging smaller non-overlapping slots, including style updates, axis changes and reparent cleanup; matching native/source repair is retained in tools/platform-qualification/patches/windows-layout/. The adopted preview must also include null invalid custom properties and whole-value variable invalidation from NativeScript#11527/#11593.

patches.why: useEditor.ts reads bare process.env.NODE_ENV — no node global exists in the harness typecheck program. Adds a module-local process declaration for typecheck. (The './Context' self-import half of the 0.0.51 patch shipped upstream in 0.0.52 via octanejs/octane#1502.)
patches.dropWhen: @octanejs/tiptap declares process ambiently in useEditor.ts (closed unmerged upstream) or the leaf stops typechecking its raw sources

patches.why: @nativescript/doctor's Android runtime check reads the app's raw devDependencies specifier and npm dist-tag resolves anything that isn't a semver range — a pnpm `catalog:` pin throws 'The determined Android runtime version ... is not valid' and kills `ns build android` before toolchain checks. Resolve catalog specifiers through the installed package's manifest, reusing the existing tgz-branch mechanism.
patches.dropWhen: @nativescript/doctor resolves non-registry specifiers (catalog:, workspace:, link:) to the installed package version, or nativescript stops gating `ns build` on it.

patches.why: @tsrx/core's parser crashes on `const` type parameters inside type-literal signatures — tsFillSignature calls tsTryParseTypeParameters() without the modifier parser, so call signatures, method signatures, and function-type expressions carrying `<const T>` throw `Unexpected keyword 'const'` (typed-router generics like @octane-xplat/ui's RouteGroupDefiner hit this). Passes tsParseConstModifier through, matching function-declaration handling. Applies to a transitive dep of @tsrx/core — no app declares it directly.
patches.dropWhen: Upstream acorn-typescript passes tsParseConstModifier to tsTryParseTypeParameters in tsFillSignature, so `const` type parameters parse in type-literal call signatures, method signatures, and function-type expressions.

patches.why: Each NSSqliteBridge.xcframework slice ships a bare Headers/module.modulemap declaring `module NSSqlite`, so Xcode's ProcessXCFramework declares .../include/module.modulemap as its output — the same fixed path SwiftPM's FontManager.xcframework binary target emits, failing iOS builds with 'Multiple commands produce .../include/module.modulemap'. The map only enables `import NSSqlite` in Swift/ObjC sources; NativeScript reaches the NSSqliteBridge ObjC class through runtime metadata generated from the retained headers, so deleting it costs nothing in-app.
patches.dropWhen: Upstream renames or drops the per-slice modulemap (or ships a framework-style xcframework) so ProcessXCFramework no longer emits include/module.modulemap alongside another modulemap-carrying library xcframework.

patches.why: Published 6.2.0 declares playbackStartEvent but never emits it on either platform. Android: onPlayWhenReadyChanged only marks eventPlaybackStart on a play request, so the flag neither reports actual playback nor prevents a missing start; the patch emits playbackStart once per source from onIsPlayingChanged — ExoPlayer's actual-playing transition (READY + playWhenReady + unsuppressed) — keeping release()/non-loop-ended flag resets so replays and source replacements report again, and returning onPlayWhenReadyChanged to a stub so a request during buffering cannot surface as a start. iOS: playbackStart() is dead code with no call site — PlayerObserverClass only watches item 'status' for playbackReady; the patch observes the player's KVO-compliant 'timeControlStatus' and emits once per source from its Playing state (AVFoundation's actual-playing transition — a buffering player reports WaitingToPlayAtSpecifiedRate), guarded by eventPlaybackStart reset on non-looping finish, item replacement, and _setNativePlayerSource so replays and replacements report again while looping does not; the player-state observer attaches in _init(), re-attaches when the AVPlayer instance is replaced, and detaches in destroy(). The patch also pauses the shared AVPlayer on source replacement when autoplay is off: AVPlayer.rate survives replaceCurrentItemWithPlayerItem, so a player told to play would otherwise resume on the next item even when the new source requests autoplay=false (Android recreates its ExoPlayer per source, resetting playWhenReady). Callback delivery on Android additionally requires the NativeScript runtime default-interface-override repair tracked under octane-xplat#220.
patches.dropWhen: An upstream release emits playbackStart from an actual playback transition — isPlaying or first rendered frame on Android, timeControlStatus Playing or equivalent on iOS — rather than a play request or a dead emitter, or the leaf stops consuming the plugin event.
